Container.Name: print-handy

Branch.TagDescription: Stable. A fixed release, the recommended choice for a printer you rely on. A new release does not move this tag; to update, change the Repository tag to the newer version number.
Development build, rebuilt nightly from main after the full CI suite passes. Features may be unfinished and settings may change without a release note.

Development build that follows main automatically, ahead of nightly. For testing current fixes before they reach nightly or a release; features may be unfinished and settings may change without a release note.

Container.Overview: Share a model link or file in Discord, Telegram or Matrix. Choose filament, review the estimate and approve the exact job before it reaches your printer. Runs locally with no Print Handy cloud; chat providers carry what you send, and model downloads or optional hosted AI use the network. Camera monitoring and AI features are optional. A camera alert is not proof that a print is safe unattended. See the printer support guide for supported connection paths and hardware verification limits. Not affiliated with Bambu Lab. SETUP: all data lives in the one Appdata folder, and that folder must be writable by UID 1000 (the container user). Before the first start, run in the Unraid terminal: chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/print-handy. To use a chat bot, put its token in state/.env inside that folder (for example DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=... or TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=...) before the first start. Then open the Web UI on port 8088 to finish setup. The Web UI is open to anyone on your network until you set a password there. Full setup and upgrade instructions are in the Print Handy docs: https://catduckgnaf.github.io/print-handy-docs/ (Docker setup guide: https://github.com/catduckgnaf/print-handy/blob/main/docs/DOCKER.md).
Container.Requires: Appdata path and every child data folder must be owned by UID/GID 1000. Before upgrading an existing installation from the single /data bind template, stop the container and back up its appdata and container. Images before 2.2.9 declared child volumes under /data, so an install created on one of them may have stored state in anonymous volumes instead of the Appdata folder. 2.2.9 and later declare none, but upgrading does not move data out of those existing volumes. Copy each existing child volume's contents into the matching folder under Appdata (state, hermes, archive, records, cache, spoolman) before recreating the container; do not remove old container or volumes until the new install is verified. Keep existing /data/.config contents: account tokens are stored there. If an older template mapped them to a host folder named dot-config, rename it to .config (mv dot-config .config) so the tokens and Web UI settings are found. Keep the separate Timelapse Archive host mapping unchanged. No automatic migration occurs.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Host port for the Print Handy Web UI. If port 8088 is already in use by another service or Docker container on your server, change this host port.

Config.Name: Appdata Storage
Config.Description: Parent appdata folder. Images before 2.2.9 declared child volumes below /data; the explicit child paths below keep those directories on the host for installs created on those images. 2.2.9 and later declare no volumes, and the child paths stay harmless there. The folder must be owned by UID/GID 1000: chown -R 1000:1000 /mnt/user/appdata/print-handy.

Config.Name: State Storage
Config.Description: Persistent current state directory. Preserve existing contents when changing this mapping.

Config.Name: Legacy State Storage
Config.Description: Legacy state location used by installations created before Print Handy 2.2.5. Keep existing contents; the image supports migration from this path.

Config.Name: Archive Storage
Config.Description: Persistent archive data. Preserve existing contents when changing this mapping.

Config.Name: Records Storage
Config.Description: Persistent records data. Preserve existing contents when changing this mapping.

Config.Name: Cache Storage
Config.Description: Persistent cache data. Preserve existing contents when changing this mapping.

Config.Name: Spoolman Storage
Config.Description: Bundled Spoolman database. Copy any existing Spoolman data here before starting; do not overwrite existing files.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Account tokens and related user configuration. Preserve existing contents and file ownership.

Config.Name: Timelapse Archive
Config.Description: Finished timelapses are copied here. The default folder is inside Appdata; point this at another share (for example a media share) to keep timelapses somewhere else.

Config.Name: Container Timezone
Config.Description: IANA timezone for the container's local time (e.g. America/New_York, Europe/London, America/Chicago). Sets the container's local time: log timestamps and scheduled jobs. Chat display times follow the discord.timezone setting, not this one.

Config.Name: Hardware Acceleration (Intel / AMD)
Config.Description: OPTIONAL: Direct Rendering Infrastructure (/dev/dri) device pass-through for hardware-accelerated timelapse encoding on Intel (QuickSync / VA-API) or AMD (VA-API). Requires GPU drivers installed on Unraid. The entry ships empty so hosts without an iGPU still start; to enable it, set the value to /dev/dri. The container runs as UID 1000, so it also needs access to the render group: add --group-add=GID to Extra Parameters (see the Docker setup guide, GPU passthrough).

Config.Name: NVIDIA Visible Devices
Config.Description: OPTIONAL (NVIDIA GPUs only): GPU UUID (e.g. GPU-xxxxxxxx) or 'all' for NVENC timelapse encoding. Requires the Unraid Nvidia-Driver plugin and '--runtime=nvidia' added to Extra Parameters.

Config.Name: NVIDIA Driver Capabilities
Config.Description: OPTIONAL (NVIDIA GPUs only): Driver libraries the NVIDIA runtime mounts. Default is compute,video,utility (or all).
